data.name: Tutorial.Intro
data.value:
Nera adds an experimental DLDR display mode to Windows.
Turn on DLDR, then continue using Windows normally. DLSS5 neural rendering and DLDR preserve an HDR display pipeline.
Nera does not modify app or game files, the graphics driver, or the NVIDIA runtime file on disk. Experimental compatibility runs inside Nera’s isolated host.

data.name: Tutorial.Checks
Tutorial.Use
data.value:
1. Click DLDR. 2. Wait for DLDR ON in the center of the screen. 3. Use pictures, video, the desktop, or games normally. 4. Click DLDR again, or use your shortcut, to turn it off.
Reopen Nera from the taskbar or your shortcut to adjust the picture without turning DLDR off.

data.value: Ctrl + Alt + Backspace is always reserved as the emergency-stop fallback. Check its actual registration below.

data.name: Tutorial.Measured
data.value: Available local sample: DLSS5 processing averaged {0:F2} ms. This is not a full stability benchmark.

data.name: Tutorial.NotMeasured
data.value: No local quick-test result is available yet. The options below are starting suggestions, not verified performance results.

data.name: Tutorial.Recommendations
data.value:
4K at 60 FPS: consider Balanced (90%). GPU-heavy games: try Smooth (80%). Still pictures or lower-frame-rate content: try Quality (100%).
Final output always stays at the selected display resolution.

data.value: Recommendations use only available local quick-test evidence. They do not guarantee performance and are never applied automatically. You can adjust them at any time. DLDR remains OFF when you finish.
